archival_memory.user_research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year, and it's been an eye-opening experience. It's given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world, and I'm glad to be a part of it. I was initially hesitant to take the leap, but it turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.user_lab_description: The lab I'm in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with scientists from various backgrounds to make massive amounts of data more comprehensible. We deal with datasets that are tens of terabytes in size, and my main task is working on front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards. I use advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if needed.
archival_memory.user_first_project: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. The raw data was enormous, consisting of daily temperature readings from buoys around the Pacific. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to explore specific regions or timeframes. The project culminated in co-authoring my first paper, which was a surreal and proud moment in my college journey.
archival_memory.user_current_project: I'm currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can enhance scientists' understanding of complex data. By creating 3D representations of data in virtual environments, scientists can interact with the data in a more intuitive way, such as walking around, touching, and highlighting subsets. This is a significant leap from traditional data visualization methods like coding websites or using 2D visuals. The process involves experimentation, integrating VR headsets, and using engines like Unity or Unreal to efficiently stream data into the 3D environment. It's a cutting-edge field, and every day, I'm forging my own path as there isn't a well-established best-practice library for VR data visualization yet.
archival_memory.user_research_life: Research life is not just about coding away in a quiet corner. It's a lot of reading, especially academic papers. When solving a bug with volumetric data rendering in VR, I need to search for similar attempts in conference proceedings or workshops. It can be overwhelming, but I've learned to skim effectively by looking at abstracts, introductions, and conclusions. Occasionally, I share interesting discoveries with the lab and we discuss how to incorporate those techniques into our workflow.
archival_memory.user_lab_collaboration: I have the opportunity to interact with graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first due to their deep immersion in niche fields. However, it's also inspiring to see their expertise and passion. One PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets and integrating it with our VR platform. This will allow us to display a compressed representation of datasets like climate data, reducing the need for full loading in VR. It's fascinating to see theoretical concepts applied in practical ways. Our best brainstorming sessions often happen spontaneously, like in the lab break room, where we discuss how to offload processing to the GPU while sipping coffee.
archival_memory.user_poster_presentations: I've had the opportunity to present our research through poster presentations at smaller symposiums around campus. It's a great experience that requires distilling complex research into easy-to-understand visuals and talking points. Initially, I was nervous about presenting, but it turned out to be a friendly dialogue with genuine interest from the audience. I even met a few folks from local startups who shared interesting perspectives on how VR for data visualization could benefit commercial industries like marketing analytics or architecture. It opened my eyes to the potential for research to transition from academia to real-world applications.
archival_memory.user_publications: I've been fortunate enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a larger conference submission for the IEEE Visualization Conference. Our research focuses on comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment in a user study. We hypothesize that VR immersion helps researchers spot anomalies or trends faster than 2D charts. We conducted a small user trial with 15 participants, recording their times and gathering UX feedback. Now, we're analyzing the data to determine if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a collaborative effort, with each of us handling specific sections. It's a balancing act, especially with senior coursework and a capstone project to manage.
archival_memory.user_future_plans: I'm currently considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master's or PhD. I believe that contributing to cutting-edge knowledge in areas like data visualization or machine learning is very appealing. However, I also want to see how these concepts are applied in real product development. One of my mentors suggested that stepping into industry can provide a better understanding of what problems are truly relevant, which would be beneficial if I decide to return for a PhD with a more practical approach.
archival_memory.user_frustrations: Research can be frustrating at times, with weeks spent on approaches that don't pan out or discovering that existing ideas have already been done and improved upon by others. However, the key is to adapt and incorporate new findings into our work. We read existing papers, think of new angles or applications, and push the boundaries of what's been done before. The essence of research lies in building on the foundation of what others have accomplished. The sense of collaboration within our lab and among the global research community is truly special.
archival_memory.user_lab_crisis: A few months ago, one of our massive servers crashed, and we lost vital data that wasn't fully backed up. The scramble to recover the data was intense, with frantic email chains and Zoom calls with the lab manager. Fortunately, we were able to restore most of the data, but the crisis highlighted the importance of data backups. We learned from the experience and set up a better backup system to prevent such a disaster in the future. It was a stressful event, but it also brought the lab together and taught us valuable lessons.
archival_memory.user_professor_connection: Research has allowed me to connect with professors on a more personal level, beyond just being a student in their classes. My PI is very approachable and supportive, offering guidance on career direction and helping me with external opportunities. I've been recommended for various scholarships, events, and networking opportunities, which have been valuable experiences. One such event was a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I met experts from around the world debating technical details and proposing new frameworks. It was fascinating to see the frontier of CS knowledge unfolding in real time.
archival_memory.user_journey: My journey in the research world has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the feeling that my work in the lab could shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive technologies we're pioneering might one day become standard tools, and I'd be proud to have been part of that from the beginning. The sense of contributing to something bigger keeps me motivated. This experience has changed how I think about computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the perspectives I've gained.
